articles.title: Design for density, not visual noise
articles.author: Editorial Team
paragraphs: Useful software often has more information than a marketing page. The visual system should help readers distinguish navigation, active work, context, and supporting metadata without placing every sentence inside a thick border.

The page remains legible by varying the strength of separators, limiting accent colors, and keeping a consistent typographic rhythm. Interactive controls retain clear focus and selection states, even when their default treatment is understated.
A shared design system should translate across applications without forcing identical page compositions. Content hierarchy is a contract; the amount of whitespace can respond to the task.

articles.title: A practical guide to design tokens
articles.author: Documentation Team
paragraphs: Tokens describe purpose rather than appearance. A canvas, a panel and a nested record must stay distinct across all available themes. Colors are only one of several dimensions of hierarchy.
Component states should be visible in the gallery alongside the full-page examples. This helps reveal broken disabled, hover and focus treatments that are harder to notice in a polished screenshot.

quote.text: An interface can be dense without feeling heavy.

faq.question: Is this a UI framework?
faq.answer: No. The Mechanics is a portable visual standard and demonstration environment.

faq.question: Do themes affect component sizes?
faq.answer: No. Themes change color and surface treatment, not geometry or behavior.

faq.question: Can an application use only the CSS?
faq.answer: The output should document a CSS-only integration path where feasible.

callout.heading: Accessibility first
